defects.what: The wall is held by a thicket of arms that belong to nobody: a long pale-orange arm runs the full height of the frame with no shoulder, and at least four more forearms and hands sprout from behind the planks with no body attached.
The kapre's belly forms a complete second face: brow shadow, a dark triangular nose, a moustache and a mouth/chin above the blue sarong.
Same still as k46: the kapre's belly forms a second face.

The mirror reflection does not match the man: the reflection has a neat bun, no grey streak and a red kerchief tied on the wrist, while the man himself has a spiky topknot with a grey streak and no kerchief.
The two clasped hands run together into one knot of fingers with two thumbs and no readable wrist on the lower hand; it cannot be told which finger belongs to whom.
Sinag has long silver hair and an open low-cut white suit; in k50, k51 and k53 she has black hair and a closed high-collared white outfit.
Same still as k49: Sinag with silver hair and low-cut suit, unlike her other shots.
Vangie has orange-brown hair, no glasses and a blue blazer with a tie; in k29, k31, k33, k34 she is black-haired, wears glasses and a khaki shirt.
The man in the suit (Tubal) is a grinning twenty-something with spiky hair and a round face, not the slicked-back fifty-year-old of k15, k19, k20 and k26.
Two warriors in the front rank are the same man copied: same spiky topknot and ponytail, same bare torso, same face turned the same way, same shield.

The kapre is a bare-skinned, light-brown muscular giant in grey shorts, while one shot earlier (k46) he is covered head to foot in dark brown fur with a blue sarong; the cut reads as two different creatures.
Sinag's hand around the wine glass is a soft pale smear without readable fingers.
First reader called the handshake a lump of merged fingers with a floating ring.
defects.second_reader: refuted: at 3x it is an ordinary handshake - one thumb and the knuckles of each hand are readable, no extra or fused fingers, and the ring sits on a finger of the lower hand.
